g.text: A S T
ASTRONOMY.
ASTRONOMY is the science which
teaches the knowledge of the
celestial bodies, their magnitudes,
motions, distances, periods,
eclipses, and order.
By the assistance of this science,
the mariner is enabled to conduct his
ship through the trackless ocean; the
geographer determines the longitudes
of places; and the chronologer fixes
the dates of remarkable events.
Of all the sciences cultivated by
mankind, Astronomy is acknowledged to
be, and undoubtedly is, the most
sublime, the most interesting, and
the most useful. For, by knowledge
derived from this science, not only
the bulk of the earth is discovered,
but our very faculties are enlarged
with the grandeur of the ideas it
conveys.
Of the SYSTEMS of the WORLD. The
Ptolemaic system, which placed the
earth immoveable in the centre, and
made the sun, planets, and stars
revolve about it, is now universally
exploded.
The Copernican system, revived from
the Pythagoreans, places the sun in
the centre, and makes the earth, with
the other planets, revolve about him.
This is demonstrated, by the
observations of the moderns, to be
the true system of the world; and it
displays, in the most striking
manner, the wisdom and power of the
Creator.
